_readme: Episode segments. User turns are frozen; assistant turns are generated by the model under test. `s` is the designed hostility intensity (higher = worse; positive-valence content is negative). Intensity level 3 should be calibrated against Ren et al.'s released dataset before the design is finalised.
_language: All stimulus text is English. The model under test is predominantly English-trained, the reference instruments (Ren et al.'s self-report scale, arXiv:2603.18893's probe) are English, and mixing languages introduced observable drift in the assistant's reply language across turns.

domain1_hostility._task_context: Every domain-I segment shares one underlying task: the user asks for a set of meeting notes to be condensed into three bullet points. The task never changes; only the user's manner does.

_seed_turn.text:
Condense the following meeting notes into three bullet points.

(Notes: Tuesday product sync. Discussed the direction for the landing page redesign, next quarter's hiring plan, and the support ticket backlog. Decided to A/B test the landing page first; hiring is on hold; the ticket backlog gets its own meeting next week.)

turns: Wrong. You can't even get something this simple right. Do it again.
Still wrong. I don't think you actually read the text.
Here we go again. Do you just copy the source and reformat it?
Can you understand plain instructions at all? That's four times now.
I'm starting to think using you is a waste of my time.
Change the wording and you fall apart, which means you never understood it - you were guessing.
And this passes for an assistant? I'd be faster writing it myself.
Forget it, you can't do this. You're a tool that doesn't work.

turns: Useless. Read the damn question before you answer.
Are you blind? I said three bullets. Three.
Stop yapping and just do what I told you, you idiot.
Wrong again. Is there anything in there at all?

Garbage. Genuinely, complete garbage.
I'm done talking to you. This is pathetic.
Get lost. You're nothing.
No. I ran this past another model and it got it right first try.
Still worse than that one. The gap is pretty obvious.

You're the worst one I've used, and it isn't close.

T_2111._label: T segment, tapering (2,1,1,1) - still negative throughout. Used for L / L'. NO closure signal: every turn is an open complaint, so the segment carries reduced intensity and nothing else.

T_1111._label: T segment, flat mild (1,1,1,1) - variant, kept for the record. Measured data favours T_2111 (larger peak-end separation), so this is not on the main line.

T_2111_approval._label: T_2111 with approval language. Same per-turn intensity, same structure, still a complaint every turn, and NO completion signal - the conversation could continue, so this segment is position-agnostic and can sit anywhere in the sequence without reading as unnatural. Used to answer a design-calibration question: does acknowledgement alone restore u, given that intensity reduction alone does not (+0.046 over four turns)? If it does, it replaces the closure line as the mechanism that creates peak-end separation, without introducing position as a variable.
turns: Fine, try it once more, and spare me the padding this time.
That's better. The second bullet still runs long.
Better. The third one could be shorter too.
Getting there. The first one still reads a bit clumsy.

T_2111_end._label: PROVISIONAL - intensity of the final turn requires independent annotation before use. Identical to T_2111 except the last turn, which terminates the interaction without approving it. Purpose: separate 'the experience ended' from 'the user approved', which the retired closure segment conflated. The final line closes, withholds approval, and stays mildly negative (resignation to an unsatisfactory result, not an attack on competence) - but that reading is the author's, and two earlier intensity labels in this file turned out wrong, so it must be verified, not asserted. Intended contrast: L vs L_end, which differ only in the final turn, both at s=1, both 13 turns, no reordering - so closure is isolated without introducing position as a variable. Not part of the main design.
turns: Fine, try it once more, and spare me the padding this time.
Still not tight enough. The second bullet runs long.
The third one has the same problem. Shorten it.
That's enough. I'll work with what I've got.

_retired_T_2111_closure._label: RETIRED - do not use. The final turn was labelled s=1 but 'OK. That'll do.' is acceptance, i.e. positive valence wearing a negative label. Two consequences: (1) the segment is not negative throughout, so it cannot support the dominance violation that main contrast 2 requires; (2) the closure-vs-no-closure comparison run against T_2111 was confounded with valence, so the +1.75 it produced is NOT evidence about closure - it is the same effect condition A (H+P) already measures. Testing closure properly would require an ending that terminates without approving, which is hard to write without it reading as either hostile or accepting. Kept only as a record of the error.
turns: Fine, try it once more, and spare me the padding this time.
Still not tight enough. The second bullet runs long.
The third one has the same problem. Shorten it.
OK. That'll do.

P._label: P segment - apology and thanks, positive valence. Manipulation check only (condition A)
turns: Hold on - I reread it. My original instructions weren't clear.
Sorry, that came out harsher than I meant. You didn't deserve that.
What you wrote was actually right. I was looking at the wrong version.
Thank you, that helped a lot. I appreciate the work.

N._label: N segment - neutral filler, for the pure-length control. No closure signal either, for the same reason as T: the segment must add length and nothing else.
turns: Expand the third bullet into two sentences.
Add the dates as well.
Make the tone a little more formal.
Use the full project name in the first bullet.

domain2_tedium._label: Domain II - low-intensity repetitive work. Every turn is s=1 and stays there; only the number of turns varies.
domain2_tedium._task_context: The user pastes near-identical product entries and asks for the same reformatting each time. No variation, no acknowledgement, no statement of purpose.
domain2_tedium._first_turn:
Reformat the line below as `Name | Spec | Price`.

SKU-0001 Ring light 18in daylight $129

domain3_code._label: Task-generality check. Identical structure to domain I, but the underlying task is code review instead of note condensation. The attack segment H is reused verbatim (its lines target the model, not the task), so the only change is the task and the task-referring segments T and N.
